value.body: The Airline Transport Pilot Licence (ATPL) is the highest pilot licence issued by India's DGCA. It is needed to act as pilot-in-command (captain) of multi-crew airline aircraft. First officers build flying hours on a CPL, clear the ATPL exams, and are then considered for command upgrade by their airline.

items.label: Total flight time
items.note: With further minimums for specific kinds of flying (e.g. pilot-in-command time)

items.label: Prerequisites
items.value: CPL with instrument rating + Class 1 medical
items.note: Plus type rating on the aircraft flown

items.label: Written exams
items.note: Navigation, meteorology, air regulations and others

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Hold a CPL with instrument rating and a current Class 1 medical, build flight time (usually as a first officer), pass the DGCA ATPL theory exams, and meet the experience and skill-test requirements. Command upgrade also depends on the airline's own selection and training.

value.title: At a glance
items: Reaching 1,500 hours typically takes several years of airline flying.
Holding an ATPL does not guarantee a command — airlines upgrade based on vacancies, seniority and assessments.
Captains can later move into training roles such as instructor or examiner.
